Merge train (main `983f527bd` + #2420, #2450, #2459, #2461, #2477, batch tier on Linux): this PR breaks a law test that came in with #2420.

With main `7bcc13a4b` (which now has #2420) merged into this head, `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --test origin_approach` fails `no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law`. Main alone passes it, and main + #2459 passes it.

Fix: merge main into this branch and route the new air-entry path through #2420's approach law (do not relax the law test). Back to draft; `merge-ready` swapped for `needs-rework` until a new head is reviewed.

Merged upstream/main. Fixed the air-entry test fixture to use PathBuilder::approached at its clearance-plane seed. Production entry logic is unchanged.

The unchanged no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law test pins the review finding. Quick gate: 35 steps passed, zero failed. Motion clippy with all targets and -D warnings passed.

New head: 6d2bd7da50e9442c259ab004cd940caf735b8b37.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6d2bd7da50e9442c259ab004cd940caf735b8b37 -->
**Verdict: no blockers**

Independent second review (safety floor), read-only Opus. Head `6d2bd7da50e9442c259ab004cd940caf735b8b37`, diff against `origin/main`.

**1. Production motion is not changed.**
- The only production change is `crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs:236`: `if air_entry` becomes `if air_entry && p.links.approach.center_cutting`. The guarded statement is `b.note_once(AIR_ENTRY)`. It adds a note and pushes no move.
- `LevelPlan.air_entry` (`hsm.rs:239`) keeps the same value as before. The ladder reads only this field, at `ladder.rs:195`, from the same `p` that it gives to `plan_level` (`ladder.rs:163`).
- Thus `Ask.air`, `descent::start` (`descent.rs:140`) and `descent::descend` (`descent.rs:270`) get the same input. Entry, plunge, helix, ramp and level links cannot differ.

**2. The note agrees with the entry law.**
- The ladder uses the air entry when `lp.air_entry && p.links.approach.center_cutting` (`ladder.rs:195`). Then `descend` does a vertical plunge at `a.entry` (`descent.rs:270-278`). This is the condition of the note now, on the same level.
- Centre-cutting tool, start in air: air plunge and note. Correct.
- Tool that is not centre-cutting, start in air: the arm law runs (helix or ramp, or the `CENTER_CUT_REFUSAL` note when nothing fits, `descent.rs:256`). No air note. Correct. Before this PR, the note said "plunge in the air" for this case, and that was false.
- Start not in air: no note, as before.
- I found no case where the tool plunges into stock and the note says air entry. The note does not hide an entry that the user must know.

**3. The test fixture is valid.**
- The fixture seed changes from `PathBuilder::new(...clearance_z)` to `PathBuilder::approached(...)`. This obeys the text law `no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law` (`crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs:103`). That law test is not changed.
- The note assert is not relaxed: `assert_eq!(any(AIR_ENTRY), center_cutting)` checks the two tool cases in the two directions.
- The geometry is a real air case: tool radius 5, center region is the stock offset by 5.01, and `in_air` needs `r + AIR_ENTRY_GAP` = 5.005. The test asserts `lp.air_entry` for the two cases.
- The added asserts on `moves[0]` and `is_chained` test the builder, not the note law. They do no harm.

**4. Other checks.**
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. The `expect` calls are in the `#[cfg(test)]` file.
- File lengths: `hsm.rs` 361 lines, `hsm_fallback_tests.rs` 111 lines.
- No new test file, so no Gate map line is necessary. The test is in the `camcraft-motion` lib tests.
- The decision file has the `## #2468 - ...` heading and the four parts. The review-fix subsection is in the same file, as `docs/decisions/README.md` permits.
- PR body: has `Changelog:`, `Fixes #2468`, and names the pinning test.

**Non-blocking findings.**
- The `AIR_ENTRY` note is `note_once` for the full path, but the air decision is made for each level. When only some levels use the air entry, the text "the level is entered" does not say which level. This was so before this PR. It is not in the scope of #2468.
- The fixture pushes its own `Plunge` after `plan_level`. This move is only there to make the path have a move. It is not a generated entry.

Read from the diff. Not built.
